notes.text: Captives — There were two carryings into Babylon, the latter about eleven or twelve years after the former, the first was in the time of Jehoiakim, When the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths were carried away.

glossa.text:
*And these. ((HIER.))* He purposes to persuade them not to yield to the false prophets, who were promising them a return to Jerusalem after a short time. But let them know that they will tarry a long time in Babylon.

 *The words of the book. ((ID.))* This little book of Jeremias, etc., *as far as* he might urge upon the people the things which had been commanded him by the Lord.

*To the residue of the ancients.* First to the elders, then to the priests, thirdly to the prophets, fourthly to all the people, the word of God is directed, so that according to the order of age the prophet's letter may be sent.

notes.text: All lands — Ye people of all nations. He invites the Gentile world, to the contemplation and celebration of God's works.
We — Our nation, or our ancestors, in whose loins we then were.
Proved us — As it were in a burning furnace; and with a design to purge out our dross.
Net — Which our enemies laid for us.
To ride — To use us like slaves.

glossa.text: *Shout with joy to God, all the earth,* etc. ((CAS.)) First he admonishes all to rejoice over the resurrection of Christ, which gives life to all.

*Give ye glory.* ((AUG.)) Not as the Jews, who give justice to their own merits, and envy the Gentiles their grace. *How terrible. ((Ibid.))* If thou rejoicest, fear also, lest what has been given to the humble be taken away from the proud: as was done to the Jews. Do not therefore insult over the broken branches, but fear, lest perchance he spare not thee either. *Thy works, O Lord.* ((CAS.)) Briefly he calls the mysteries of the incarnation works, that God is man, that he suffered, died, and the like. *In the multitude of thy strength.* ((AUG.)) Here he hints at the resurrection, to which, the lying Jews being shut out, the Gentiles are admitted.

((BEDA.)) The Lord rose again; many believed in him, etc., *as far as* they drank through grace. *They shall lie.* They are works of the earth, which the enemies belie, against those who lie, *let all the earth adore,* etc. ((AUG.)) *They shall lie.* Enemies are wont to lie, etc., *as far as* let all the earth adore.

*Come ye.* ((CAS.)) Diapsalma. He invites beginners to consider the works of God, that one faith may join those whom one reward awaits: where, setting forth those works, he plainly says that the resurrection pertains to the Gentiles *ressurrectionem*, the Jews being repressed.

*Who turneth. ((Ibid.))* The works in which he is terrible, and what they are, he subjoins: *Who turneth the sea.* In the river Jordan according to the letter, mystically in the passing world. *In the river. ((Ibid.))* Although sins are forgiven, yet in the course of mortality they are still there, for immortality is not at once *immortalitai*.

 *In the river.* ((AUG.)) The river is the mortality of the world, where some come and others depart: but he who believes in Christ passes over on foot, humble in himself, not on horseback and proud. *There we shall rejoice. ((Ibid.))* Or thus: The works are terrible, etc., *as far as* and in these Christians rejoice. *In him. ((Ibid.))* When he shall be all in all, or in him who rules, in his own strength.
*Let them not be exalted. ((Ibid.))* On account of the law, as though more were owed to them. *For all have sinned,* etc. ((Rom. III.))

*Bless ye.* ((CAS.)) Diapsalma. He admonishes the Gentiles to bless God, who, although he tries them by tribulations, yet leads them to the kingdom; for these things seem to stand in the way of the promised resurrection. *Make ye heard.* ((AUG.)) Openly, so that he who loves God loves his neighbour also. *The voice of his praise.* Which the Father speaks of the Son: *This is my Son.*

*Who hath set my soul. ((Ibid.))* Here he enumerates for what causes he ought to be preached.

 *For thou hast proved us.* [n: (AUG.)] Thou hast not given us over unto commotion. Because thou hast proved us, thou hast not cast us headlong, thou hast proved us by adversities, by the fire of charity, which does not suffer us to feel torments, or, thou hast tried us by the fire of tribulation, etc.
*A snare.* ((AUG.)) Not one that deceives, but one that proves. *We have passed over.* ((CAS.; AUG.)) Thou all these things, and we, etc., *as far as* this happens to us in temptations.

notes.text: Of the seed of David — This one genealogy attend to.
Is not bound — Not hindered in its course.

Therefore — Encouraged by this, that "the word of God be not bound." I endure all things - See the spirit of a real Christian? Who would not wish to be likeminded? Salvation is deliverance from all evil; glory, the enjoyment of all good.
Dead with him — Dead to sin, and ready to die for him.
If we deny him — To escape suffering for him.
If we believe not — That is, though some believe not, God will make good all his promises to them that do believe. He cannot deny himself - His word cannot fail.
Remind them — Who are under thy charge. O how many unnecessary things are thus unprofitably, nay hurtfully, contended for.

A workman that needeth not to be ashamed — Either of unfaithfulness or unskilfulness. Rightly dividing the word of truth - Duly explaining and applying the whole scripture, so as to give each hearer his due portion. But they that give one part of the gospel to all (the promises and comforts to unawakened, hardened, scoffing men) have real need to be ashamed.

glossa.text: *Be mindful.* Labour as I do, and this in the hope of eternal life. But he calls these things to mind not for Timothy's sake, but for the sake of the heretics whom he foresaw would come and would deny these things.

*As an evildoer.* Here he notes the contumely which was heaped upon him. *But the word of God is not bound.* As if he should say: Although therefore I am bound in body, yet the word of God is not bound: I who cease not to teach both those present by speech and those absent by letters.
*Salvation,* etc., *with glory,* etc. As if he should say: You have been justified that here you may obtain salvation, and, after this life, heavenly glory.
*A faithful saying.* It is this, that they shall obtain salvation and glory, for we are dead to the world, as Christ to the old man, and enduring, that is, martyrs.

*Put them in mind of these things.* That thou mayest suffer these things foretold, I put thee in mind. Or, put thine own in mind of these things. *For it is profitable to nothing.* Contention, being less stable, often begets scruple. For in contention such things are wont to be objected, the argument of ill-will being polished, that they may stir the minds of unwise brethren. Nor can it be but that contention wrings out something that is spoken against conscience, so that within, in the mind, he loses, and outwardly comes off victor. For no one suffers himself to be overcome, although he knows that the things he hears are true. There ought therefore to be conference among the servants of God, not altercation.
*And it came to pass.* After the parable by which he invites to kindness and to perseverance in the diverse offices of God, the ungrateful are reproved concerning benefits bestowed.

*There met him,* etc. The lepers are heretics, who, having as it were various colours in the same body, mingle various sects, now of falsehood, now of truth, in the same preaching. But because these are shunned and removed far from the Church, they must needs cry out with a great clamour.

*Who stood,* etc. They who have sinned against the Decalogue, loving neither God (of whom they think ill) nor the neighbour, from whom they are divided, cry under the number ten to God and are healed, while in the fellowship of the Church they attain a whole and true teaching, and expound all things according to the rule of the Catholic faith, and are free of the variety of lies as of leprosy. But one gives thanks, that is, they who remain in the unity of the Church through humility; but they who, puffed up through pride, are ungrateful to him who cleansed them, are nine, because by one unit they fall short of the perfection of the number ten.

*And they lifted up their voice.* Because they acknowledge that they have erred in the words of the Saviour, they call upon the master who is to save them, and through the knowledge of the master they return to the form of salvation.

*Go,* etc. Whoever, cleansed by the grace of God, has been rid of heretical depravity, or of Gentile superstition, or of Jewish faithlessness, or of brotherly schism, must needs come to the Church, and show a true colour of faith like to that of others.

*But one.* And the one who returned signifies the devout humility in Christ of the one Church, who, falling at his feet and giving thanks, because with the thoughts of presumption repressed he sees how weak he is, ascribes nothing of virtue to himself; the good things which he does he understands to be of mercy.

*And he fell on his face.* He falls on his face who blushes for the evils he has committed. For a man falls there where he is put to confusion. He who falls on his face sees whither he falls; he who falls backward does not see. The good therefore fall on their face, because they humble themselves in these visible things, that they may be raised to the invisible; the evil fall backward, because they fall among invisible things, where they do not see what follows them.

*Arise.* He who, acknowledging his own weakness, has lain humbly before God, is bidden by divine consolation to rise to stronger works, and to go on increasing as far as things more perfect. *Thy faith.* The faith which inclined him to give thanks; on the contrary, faithlessness condemns those who are ungrateful for benefits received. *Hath made thee whole.* In the parable above it is determined that faith ought to be increased through humility. In this one it is manifestly shown by the facts themselves, that it is not the acknowledged reason of faith only, but the executed working of faith, that makes the believer whole.

glossa.text: *Naaman,* etc. ((RAB.)) He signifies the Gentiles who bear rule by valour in war and enjoy the beauty of things. Whence Naaman is interpreted "comeliness" or "their commotion": a man valiant and rich, but a leper; because although through the power of his kingdom and the abundance of his goods he seemed to hold dominion: yet through the error of idolatry he appeared foul with leprosy.

*And out of Syria.* ((ID.)) Robbers out of Syria, etc., *as far as* as in the Gospel the prince of the priests did.

((ID.)) And the Lord *whom he foreknew, them he also called,* etc. The Gentile people coming to the house of Elisaeus, etc., *as far as* because the baptized must be confirmed by the partaking of the Lord's body.

notes.text: Sought — Diligently meditated upon.
Work — Either all his works, or that eminent branch of those works, his providence towards his people. Righteousness - His justice or faithfulness in performing his word.
Remembered — By their own nature, and the lasting benefits flowing from them, which are such as cannot easily be forgotten.
Meat — All necessary provisions for their being and well-being.

The works — All that he doth on the behalf of his people, or against their enemies. Truth - Are exactly agreeable to his promises, and to justice. Commandments - His laws given to the Israelites, especially the moral law. Sure - Constant and unchangeable.
Done — Constituted or ordered.

Redemption — The deliverance out of Egypt, which was a type of that higher redemption by Christ. Commanded - Appointed, or established firmly by his power and authority. For ever - Through all successive generations of his people to the end of the world. Reverend - Terrible to his enemies, venerable in his peoples eyes, and holy in all his dealings with all men.

The fear — True religion. Beginning - Is the only foundation of, and introduction to, true wisdom. This also is an alphabetical psalm. We have here the character and blessedness of the righteous, ver. 1-9. The iniquity of the wicked, ver. 10.

glossa.text: *I will give praise.* ((AUG.)) Here there is no confession of sins, but of praise: the one mourns, this rejoices: the one shows the wound to the physician, this gives thanks for health. *In the council.* Not rashly, but out of reason, namely for things eternal, as all the just do. ((CASS.)) *In the council of the just.* Here never among all the just, where the wicked are mingled with them, but they are seen already to sing in the fellowship to come, caught up by hope to the things above. *In the council,* which is, when they judge with the Lord. *In the congregation,* when they are gathered together out of the whole.

*Great works.* This is the matter and the cause of the confession. Great are the works of the Lord, in that he makes a godly man out of an ungodly. *Sought out.* ((AUG., CASS.)) To which nothing is like, while he suffers the devil to rage, etc., *as far as* not: *for his justice remaineth for ever and ever. Unto all the wills.* ((AUG.)) Nothing surpasses the will of God, who, even if he wills that thou sin not, yet does not prevent it. If he wills to spare the penitent, he wills also to punish the impenitent; so concerning man God always fulfils his own will, because man does nothing out of which God does not work what he wills.

*Confession and magnificence is his work.* ((CASS.)) As it were: I will give praise, because great are the works of the Lord. Any works soever are also great, if in them there be seen the intention and the will, which is the *confession* of sins, and the *magnificence* of good works: and *justice,* that is, the reward which is justly given.

*He hath made a remembrance.* ((ID.)) Secondly he says that the faithful are filled with a plentiful gift, promising the coming of the Lord, that the inheritance may be eagerly sought. ((AUG.)) *He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works.* Humbling this man and exalting that, etc., *as far as* what shall he receive, he is glorified *glorificatur*; read *glorificatus*, "glorified", in the things to come?

*He hath given food.* ((CASS.)) He makes confession and magnificence, etc., *as far as* that all things may be fulfilled. *He will be mindful,* etc. ((AUG.)) Nor did he give the whole who gave a pledge, etc., *as far as* they enter through the piercing straits of the passion.

*The power of the works.* ((CASS.)) The power of the works is that the blind see, etc. Which things he made known to the Christian people. *That he may give them the inheritance,* this was the intent of the miracles, that they might believe.

*That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles.* ((ID.)) As it were: although he gives them the inheritance, yet they shall suffer many things. *The works of his hands.* ((ID.)) That is, of his power. *Truth,* while he restores to the converted what was promised: *Judgment,* which he threatens to the ungodly. ((AUG.)) *Truth,* which the holy martyrs hold, and for which they are also judged here; *and judgment,* whereby in time to come they shall judge those by whom they are here judged. ((ID.)) *The works of his hands are truth and judgment.* Let *truth* be held by those who are judged, etc., *as far as* this is the inheritance of the New Testament.

*All the commandments are faithful.* ((CASS.)) Because they keep those who keep them, they are not lies. *Confirmed.* Not sent forth in vain, as human words are: *Made,* not only spoken, *in truth,* because all are fulfilled.

*In equity.* ((AUG.)) Because all things are done with the balance of justice.

*He hath sent redemption.* ((CASS.)) Thirdly he affirms the redeemed, and the New Testament consecrated by eternal grace; or. *His name: the beginning of wisdom.* ((ID.)) That is, the Son, who in his humanity is *holy,* in the power of the Godhead *terrible.* Let the advocate therefore be loved, let the judge be feared, lest thou be negligent, lest thou despair.

The fear of the Lord. ((ID.)) The dread of judgment is the gate of conversion, if the discernment of love be added to it. *His praise continueth.* The intent of the psalm, whence Alleluia is prefixed, began with praise and ends in praise: the faithful people, delivered from the devil and giving thanks, has expressed what is to be done here also by the devout, and to be accomplished in heaven: here because he delivers, there because he crowns.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Great are the works of the Lord.
We return to give you thanks.
Ten were healed, and one came back praising God.
We return to give you thanks.
He remembers his covenant forever.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: A foreign general dips seven times in a muddy river and comes up clean as a child.
We return to give you thanks.
Ten lepers are healed on the road, but only one turns around to fall at Jesus' feet.
We return to give you thanks.
Healing is everywhere; gratitude is rarer — and gratitude is the whole of worship.
We return to give you thanks.
So we are the one who came back, loud and unashamed, glorifying God.
We return to give you thanks!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A foreign general comes up from the river clean.
We return to give you thanks.
Ten are healed; one turns back to praise.
We return to give you thanks.
We are the one who came back, unashamed.
We return to give you thanks. Amen.
